S1.why: A bare number plus adjective is how a Croatian label names slots; genitive plural agrees with 5, the fixed free limit.

S2.why: An invitation in the vi imperative the vocabulary uses; says carry on, with no limit or warning in it.

S3.s: Iskoristili ste svih %lld besplatnih cutlinga. Ostaju besplatni i rade kao dosad.
S3.back: Used-up you-have all 5 free cutlings. They-stay free and work as till-now.
S3.why: Person as subject avoids number agreement on the verb; lowercase cutling for the item as in the vocabulary's running sentence, Cutling capitalised only as the app.

S4.why: Topic-first Croatian word order instead of a 'you can' sentence; genitive plural after 5.

S5.why: Active voice keeps the verb free of the 1 / 2-4 / 5+ agreement; 'od 5 besplatnih cutlinga' is genitive whatever the first number is, so no positional forms are needed.

S6.why: 'Mjesta za' is the everyday way to say there is room for; 24 characters with 5.000.

S7.why: Tekst and slike are the vocabulary's names for the two kinds; genitive plurals agree with both numbers.

S8.why: Croatian joins the last of three with 'i' and puts no comma before it.

S9.s: Jedna kupnja vrijedi na svim uređajima s vašim Apple računom.
S9.back: One purchase is-valid on all devices with your Apple account.
S9.why: Apple račun and lowercase vaš as in the vocabulary; kupnja is the Croatian standard word (kupovina reads Serbian).

S10.why: Plain statement in vi; 'samo jednom' carries the nothing-recurring meaning without a sales word.

S11.why: 'Nema … ni …' is the native way to list absences; registracija is the usual Croatian word for signing up, and it keeps račun for the Apple Account alone.

S12.why: The wording Croatian iOS apps use for the App Store restore action: ti-form imperative as on Croatian iOS buttons, kupnje as in iOS 'Mediji i kupnje'.

S13.why: Verbal noun is how Croatian iOS shows a process under way; ends with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: Buttons take the ti imperative like the vocabulary's Nastavi; 'jednokratno' is the word Croatian shops use for a one-off payment; 25 characters plus the price.

S15.why: The same command without the price, inside 14 characters.

S16.why: The usual polite put-off in Croatian apps; it postpones rather than refuses.

S17.why: The label Croatian iOS gives its close buttons.

S18.why: Warm and spoken; 'sad' rather than 'sada' for a lighter tone, and 'sve' covers the items and the room together.

S19.s: Hvala vam. Time podržavate Cutling i jednu osobu koja ga izrađuje.
S19.back: Thank you. With-that you-support Cutling and one person who it makes.
S19.why: 'Osoba' keeps the maker ungendered; thanks first, then what the purchase does, in two short sentences.

S20.s: Dobro došli natrag. Vaša je kupnja vraćena.
S20.back: Well come back. Your is purchase restored.
S20.why: 'Dobro došli' and 'natrag' are the Croatian forms (not dobrodošli, nazad); 'vraćena' matches Vrati kupnje; clitic 'je' in second position as standard Croatian places it.

S21.why: The same active form as S5 so VoiceOver and the screen say one thing; correct for any used count.

S22.why: The vocabulary's 'Cutlinga: %lld' pattern reads correctly for 1, 2, 5 and 21, which a noun after the number would not.

S23.s: Cutling je otključan. Ima mjesta za %@ cutlinga.
S23.back: Cutling is unlocked. There-is room for 5.000 cutlings.
S23.why: App name capitalised, item word lowercase; genitive plural after 5.000.

S24.why: 'Nije dovršena' states the fact calmly where 'nije uspjela' sounds like a failure.

S25.s: App Store trenutačno nije dostupan. Pokušajte ponovno malo kasnije.
S25.back: App Store at-the-moment not-is available. Try again a-little later.
S25.why: 'Trenutačno' is the Croatian standard form; App Store kept as subject so it needs no case ending.

S26.s: App Store nije potvrdio ovu kupnju.
S26.back: App Store not-has confirmed this purchase.
S26.why: App Store masculine as Croatian Apple text treats it; names the cause with no blame on the person.

S27.s: Na Apple računu s kojim ste prijavljeni na ovom uređaju nema kupnje Cutlinga.
S27.back: On Apple account with which you-are signed-in on this device there-is-no purchase of-Cutling.
S27.why: Croatian says a person is signed in with an account; 'earlier' is carried by the restore context so the line stays inside 80.

S28.s: Besplatna verzija prima %lld cutlinga. Otključajte Cutling jednom i spremajte koliko god želite.
S28.back: Free version takes 5 cutlings. Unlock Cutling once and save as-much ever you-want.
S28.why: 'Prima' is the everyday capacity verb (a hall takes 500 people); vi imperative for a sentence Siri speaks.

S29.why: Genitive after 'od 5' holds for any used count; 17 characters.

K1.why: Elliptical 'svih 5 je zauzeto' is how a Croatian speaker says every place is taken; the second half names what the tap does; exactly 38 characters.

M1.why: Mac window and menu commands in Croatian are ti-form imperatives (Otvori, Spremi).

M2.why: The same command as M1 with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: The vocabulary's plural Cutlinzi in sentence case for a row label.

M4.why: 'X od Y' is the compact Croatian number pair; no noun so no agreement.

M5.why: Plain status with the app name, masculine agreement.

M6.s: Jedna kupnja otključava Cutling na iPhoneu, iPadu i Macu.
M6.back: One purchase unlocks Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Device names take Croatian locative endings as Apple's Croatian text does.

M7.s: Vrijedi na iPhoneu, iPadu i Macu s ovim Apple računom.
M7.back: Is-valid on iPhone, iPad and Mac with this Apple account.
M7.why: Starts from 'vrijedi' so it does not repeat M5's 'Cutling je otključan' right above it.

M8.s: Kupili ste Cutling prije nego što je postao besplatan, pa ostaje otključan. Hvala vam.
M8.back: Bought you-have Cutling before than what is become free, so it-stays unlocked. Thank you.
M8.why: 'Pa' joins the reason the way speech does; the thanks comes last and stands on its own.
